itens.titulo: Why Intel Stock Is Down After Weak Q4 Guidance
itens.descricao: Why Intel Stock Is Down After Weak Q4 Guidance Yahoo Finance
trechos: - Intel reported Q3 2026 sales of US$16,513 million with net income of US$3,320 million, and issued Q4 guidance calling for US$15.0 billion to US$16.0 billion in revenue and US$0.10 in diluted EPS attributable to Intel.

- Management attributed the weaker Q4 outlook to soft PC demand, memory shortages, and production disruptions including a shutdown at its Israel facility, while demand for Xeon server and AI chips remained strong.
- We will now examine how Intel's weaker Q4 outlook and PC headwinds could reshape the longer term investment narrative around AI.
The big swing factor is still whether those US$20b plus annual capex levels convert into profitable Xeon and foundry volumes rather than just unused fabs that weigh on cash flow.
The Q4 reset puts a bright spotlight on that question, because it shows how quickly demand can clash with supply bottlenecks and outages.
The Oracle Cloud Infrastructure agreement around current and future Intel Xeon platforms, including the planned Diamond Rapids based X14 instances, ties directly into that catalyst and risk pair.
If Intel executes on that roadmap coordination, it could help fill upcoming 18A and packaging capacity and support the AI server narrative that underpins the capex plan.
Intel's analyst narrative points to revenues of US$97.1b and earnings of US$22.0b by 2029, anchored on 17.5% yearly revenue growth and an earnings swing of US$34.0b from a loss of US$12.0b today.

itens.titulo: Third-quarter revenue at Palantir Technologies surges 96%
itens.descricao: Third-quarter revenue at Palantir Technologies surges 96% Yahoo Finance
trechos: Third-quarter revenue at Palantir Technologies surged 96% year-over-year, the US-based software company said on Monday.
The company's revenue for the period rose to $2.313 billion from $1.181 billion last year.
Co-founder and chief executive Alex Karp said it was "an understatement" to say the quarter was extraordinary.
"We generated $984 million this past quarter in the US commercial market - a 148% increase from the same period the year before," he said.

It is a rate of expansion that represents a degree of intensity and sustained momentum that we believe is unmatched in recent economic history." The company's earnings totalled $1.128 billion, or $0.44 per share.
This compares with $475.599 million, or $0.18 per share, last year.
Excluding items, Palantir reported adjusted earnings of $1.142 billion or $0.44 per share for the period.
